subject: Clarify: We don't use customer inputs to improve models — retention windows & edge cases
messages:
From: Anya Rosen <anya@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Breuer <tomb@finlytics.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question on 'we don't train on customer data' — retention nuance

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo. Before we proceed with a pilot, Legal has a few follow-ups on your 'we don't train on customer data' statement. Two specific items we need clarified for procurement: 

1) Is customer request/response text ever used to update or fine-tune models (including internal research or offline eval sets)?
2) What is the retention policy for logs, debug snapshots, and backups — particularly for requests flagged as PII/PHI during triage?

We'd appreciate a short written statement we can attach to the SOW and a sample attestation for our compliance team.

Thanks,
Anya
Anya Rosen
Head of Legal Operations, Finlytics
anya@finlytics.com

--
Attachment: finlytics-questions.pdf (application/pdf, 28KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Anya Rosen <anya@finlytics.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question on 'we don't train on customer data' — retention nuance

Hi Anya — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; Mina and Neha are copied for technical and legal backup. I can convert this into a one-page attestation and a short appendix for the SOW by EOD tomorrow.

Summary answers (short):
- We do not use production customer request/response pairs to train, fine-tune, or update any models in our catalog. That includes both online training pipelines and offline/experimental datasets.
- Operational logs and telemetry necessary for service reliability are kept for the durations below; debug snapshots are treated as ephemeral and purged per the timeline.

Retention specifics: 
- Request/response text (customer payloads): default retention 90 days, unless customer selects the 'ephemeral' mode at onboarding (24 hours) or opts for the dedicated Private plan with pinned retention.
- Debug snapshots (full traces including raw inputs): retained up to 30 days for incident triage, then auto-deleted; customers may request immediate purge for specific sessions.
- Backups & snapshots (system-level): encrypted snapshots retained for 12 months for disaster recovery; these snapshots are not used for model training and are subject to an additional logical-separation policy (see link).
- PII/PHI flags: records flagged during triage are fast-tracked to deletion queue and masked within 48 hours; long-term backups containing flagged data are addressed via our erase procedures and customer-directed tombstoning.

I'll attach our draft attestation and the internal retention matrix. Let us know if you need the attestation notarized or a signed DocuSign flow.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

--
Attachments: redwood-nonlearning-attestation-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 54KB); retention-matrix-v3.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 16KB)

Marissa — appreciate the quick reply. A couple of clarifying follow-ups from Engineering and Procurement: 

- Is the 90-day default retention configurable per-tenant? If we move to Private (VPC) how do retention and snapshot policies change?
- For backups retained 12 months: can you confirm whether backups are encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) on the Private plan? Procurement is asking for the specific controls.
- We also need a short bullet we can paste into the SOW that says, in plain language, what "we do not train on customer data" means (one short sentence).

Thanks —
Tom
Tom Breuer
Director of Ops, Finlytics

Subject: Re: Question on 'we don't train on customer data' — retention nuance

Tom / Anya — answers inline below and attached is the attestation PDF and a short SOW-friendly sentence. Mina also included the KMS detail.

- Tenant config: yes — default is 90 days, but retention is configurable per-tenant on Dedicated and Private subscriptions. For Private (VPC/on-prem) customers you can pin retention to any value in the contract; our standard enterprise option includes a 0-90-365 slider with contractual enforcement.

- Backups & customer-managed keys: on Private deployments we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM; backups are encrypted with CMK and access logs are audited. For Hosted plans, backups are encrypted with company-managed keys and we offer Bring-Your-Own-Key on Enterprise tiers.

- One-line SOW text you can paste: "Redwood does not train, fine-tune, or incorporate customer-provided inputs into any production or research model; customer data used for debugging is ephemeral and deleted per agreed retention."

Next steps:
- I've attached redwood-nonlearning-attestation-v1.pdf for your compliance team. If you'd like it signed, we can route through DocuSign; I can also add a short appendix mapping retention types to contract clauses.

Mina / Neha — flag if any technical/legal nuance is missing.

Best,
Marissa
